To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
innovation in business service firms is associated with both explicit and tacit collective knowledge, and explicit individual knowledge.
the knowledge assets of business service firms affect their performance in terms of new service introductions and improvements to existing services.
innovation in business service firms is associated with explicit collective knowledge and tacit collective knowledge, but not with tacit individual knowledge.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of knowledge in business services innovation.
the strategic implications of organizational knowledge for business services firms.
the role of knowledge in business services innovation, and the implications of knowledge for firm performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the knowledge assets that are most conducive to innovation in business services are explicit collective knowledge and tacit collective knowledge.
the knowledge creation approaches that firms adopt are important for the performance of their innovation processes.
the firm needs to have a balance of tacitness and explicitness and of individual and collective knowledge in order to be able to innovate in business services.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the knowledge assets framework is useful in understanding the relationship between knowledge and innovation.
knowledge assets with high degrees of both tacitness and collectivenes are conducive to innovation in business services.
the creation and exploitation of knowledge in the context of business services requires an appropriate mix of tacitness and explicitness, and of individual and collective knowledge.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the knowledge assets of firms in the service industry should be viewed as an integrated set rather than as isolated entities.
knowledge creation approaches are not neutral and may lead to diverging outcomes.
firms need to be aware of the strategic value of different knowledge types and their interplay.
